attempts.label: DANDI:000689
attempts.paper_title: Li, H., Namburi, P., Olson, J.M. et al. Neurotensin orchestrates valence assignment in the amygdala. Nature 608, 586-592 (2022).
attempts.entry_title: Neurotensin and valence assignment in the amygdala (Li, Namburi, Olson et al. 2022)
attempts.summary: Almost none of the paper's main findings could be tested in this data, and none was confirmed. The dandiset holds only amygdala recordings and neurotensin sensor photometry, and no file says which mice are CRISPR or control, so the knockout behavior, anatomy, terminal photometry and group comparisons cannot be tested. The sensor's rise to sucrose after learning was significant only with all trials (p = 0.0046, against 0.093 with the first 16), and its fall to airpuff and its early dip were not reproduced. The seven functional clusters depend on an unreported smoothing window, and the units are not sorted single neurons. Behavior clustering matched only one of its two cluster counts.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Li, Namburi, Olson et al. (2022) that dandiset 000689 can hold. It holds 31 sessions of BLA recordings during the three-cue discrimination task, with pose, and the NT sensor photometry of 5 mice during reward and punishment learning. The NT sensor learning effects, the neuron and tagged-unit counts, the functional clustering and the behavior clustering are tested; the group comparisons are blocked because no file says which mice are CRISPR and which control, and the other experiments of the paper are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Li et al. (2022) from dandiset 000689

outcomes.notes: The retrograde tracing in NT::Cre;Ai14 mice is not in the dandiset, which holds BLA recordings, pose, confocal images of PVT slices from the recorded mice and NT sensor photometry. The paper names no other archive for these data.
The RNAscope images of BLA projectors are not in the dandiset.
The slice patch-clamp recordings are not in the dandiset (no intracellular data in any file).
The sequencing data of the guide RNA editing are not in the dandiset.

No in situ quantification is in the dandiset. The ecephys files of 27 mice (all but H01, H02, H07 and H08) hold stacks of 8 to 42 confocal images (COFAImages) whose descriptions name an Olympus FLUOVIEW file of the PVT (data check). The images are named only by depth, and no file says which mouse is CRISPR or control, what each image shows (channel or probe), or which cells are guide-positive, so they cannot stand in for the paper's RNAscope cell counts.
The global Nt cKO behavior cohorts (MGN, vHPC, PVT) are not in the dandiset.
The global Nt cKO tone-shock sessions are not in the dandiset.

The criterion's session reading (a), the last tone-sucrose day, is not in the dandiset (data missing); reading (b), the sucrose trials of the last discrimination day, is in the 31 recording sessions (port entries are in the trial tables), but no file says which mouse is CRISPR and which control, so no reading can be run.
The tone-shock test session of the PVT-BLA cKO cohort is not in the dandiset, which holds only discrimination-task sessions; the group labels are also missing (see fig2c).
The PVT-BLA:NT photostimulation behavior cohort is not in the dandiset.
The PVT-BLA:NT photostimulation behavior cohort is not in the dandiset.
The anticipatory licks and the eye videos of the axon-terminal photometry cohort (13 and 12 mice) are not in the dandiset. The NT sensor files hold lick events for 5 other mice but no eye video.
The PVT-BLA:NT axon-terminal GCaMP photometry is not in the dandiset; its only photometry is the GRAB-NTS1.0 sensor (fluorophore "neurotensin-fluorescent sensor", 415 and 470 nm, 5 mice).
As fig3e-terminal-sucrose-increase.
The somatic GCaMP photometry of MGN, vHPC and PVT NT neurons is not in the dandiset.
The sensor imaging in cultured neurons is not in the dandiset.

Five mice, early against late acquisition sessions as the files label them. Under the per-trial z-score (the reading adopted) the US-window response (2 to 7 s) is larger late than early under all four readings of the criterion. With all trials it is significant, AUC +3.53 (95% CI 1.82 to 5.24), t(4) = 5.74, p = 0.0046, 5 of 5 mice higher, inside the paper's CI of 2.744 to 5.538 around 4.14 (mean z +0.71, same test). With the first 16 trials it is not, AUC +2.94 (95% CI -0.77 to 6.66), t(4) = 2.20, p = 0.093, 4 of 5 mice higher. AUC and mean give the same t and p, so the two passing readings are one result. The criterion asks for p < 0.05 with late higher under every reading; it holds in 2 of the 4, so the criterion is not met, and only the direction holds in all four. The significant result also rests on the regression fitted on the trial-averaged baseline, whose correlation is 0.48 to 0.75 in four of the ten sucrose sessions (M-0 early and late, M-1 late, M-3 early). With the regression fitted on the pooled baseline bins of every trial (correlation at least 0.938) no reading reaches p < 0.05 (AUC +1.45 to +2.53, p >= 0.44), nor under the session-pooled z-score (AUC -2.92 to +0.16, p >= 0.16). The CS window does not change under any reading (p >= 0.25), as in the paper (P = 0.1483). The first run read the 470 nm channel of Mouse6's late sucrose session from the constant third frame type (see deviations); with that corrected the all-trials readings pass. Round 2 kept the outcome as partially_reproduced and proposed not_reproduced; round 3 agreed, since the criterion has no partial condition.
deviations: The files mark one kind of cue, 2 s long, and no US. All cues are taken as CS-US trials with the US 2 s after CS onset (Methods, Head-fixed behavior, "The US ... was delivered 2 s after the onset of the CS"). The Methods say about half the CSs were unpaired; in the late sucrose sessions 49 to 58 of about 60 cues are followed by licking within 2 to 5 s, so most cues are paired, but unpaired cues, if any, cannot be removed. This is an assumption.

The median filter of 200 ms is applied at the native 20 Hz before averaging into 5 Hz bins, since at 5 Hz it would do nothing (Methods, Fiber photometry, Data analysis, "down-sampled to 5Hz and filtered ... using a median filter with a span of 200 ms").

Whether the residuals are z-scored against each trial's baseline or the session's pooled baseline is not said (Methods, "Residuals from the regression were z-transformed using data a baseline window of -5 s to 0 s relative to the start of the CS"). The per-trial baseline is adopted as an assumption (each trial's own -5 to 0 s window is the plainer reading); the session-pooled one is shown and gives no p < 0.05.

The 470 nm trace is regressed on the 415 nm trace over the trial-averaged -5 to 0 s window, as the Methods say ("Regression coefficients were computed using data averaged across trials in a session"). The fitted slopes run from 0.38 to 2.33 (correlation 0.25 to 0.99); a fit on the pooled baseline bins of every trial is shown as a variant.

The single photometry series interleaves three frame types at 60 Hz where the Methods give 40 Hz. Each channel is the phase of the three-frame order that the 415 or 470 nm LED labels mark before the first irregular frame interval. In Mouse6's late sucrose session the labels move by one frame after a 2.3 ms interval while the data keep their order (phase means 0.200, 0.019 and 0.057 before and after it), so the labels there would give the constant third frame type as the 470 nm channel.

outcomes.notes: Under the per-trial z-score the US-window response to airpuff is lower late than early under all four readings (AUC -5.47, 95% CI -12.35 to 1.41, with the first 16 trials, 5 of 5 mice lower; -4.66 with all trials), near the paper's -3.657, but no reading reaches p < 0.05 (smallest p = 0.074, t(4) = -2.40). Under the session-pooled z-score p >= 0.096, and with the regression fitted on the pooled baseline bins p >= 0.23. The CS window does not change significantly under any reading (p >= 0.08), as in the paper (P = 0.0994). In Mouse1's early airpuff session (29 cues) the last three cues come 4.7 and 7.4 s apart, one a 4.7 s bout; the first-16 readings do not include them.
deviations: The files mark no airpuff, and the cue events last 2 s where the Methods give a 4 s CS. All cues are taken as CS-US trials with the airpuff 2 s after CS onset (Methods, Head-fixed behavior, "presented 2 s after the onset of the CS"). The Methods say about half the CSs were unpaired; with about 60 cues per airpuff session where the Methods give about 30 pairings, up to half the trials analysed may be unpaired, and the files cannot tell them apart. This is an assumption.

Same processing choices as fig3k-nt-sensor-sucrose-increase (median filter at 20 Hz, per-trial z-score adopted with the session one shown, regression on the trial-averaged baseline with the pooled fit shown, channels from the frame order).

outcomes.notes: In the early sessions the mean over 5 mice of the US-window z-score is below zero for sucrose (-0.62 with the first 16 trials, per-trial z-score; 3 of 5 mice below zero) but above zero for airpuff (+0.11; 4 of 5 mice are below zero, but M-4 is at +2.15). No reading has both means below zero (0 of 8). Under the session-pooled z-score with the first 16 trials the signs reverse (sucrose +0.34, airpuff -0.40). No mean differs from zero (p >= 0.23). Read as a brief dip, the lowest point of the mouse-averaged trace in 2 to 7 s is below zero for both outcomes under the per-trial z-score (-1.09 for sucrose and -0.63 for airpuff with the first 16 trials, -0.82 and -0.36 with all trials). Whether the window mean tests a "transient" decrease is asked of a reader (questions/000689.yaml); the outcome is judged on the criterion as written.
deviations: Same trial assumption and processing choices as fig3k-nt-sensor-sucrose-increase and fig3l-nt-sensor-airpuff-decrease.

outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds 31 recording sessions from 31 mice, within the tolerance of 30. It holds 1902 units; 1739 have a baseline rate (1 s before each CS) of at least 0.3 Hz, and 1884 a whole-session rate of at least 0.3 Hz. Neither unit count is within 68.5 of 685, so the mouse count holds and the neuron count does not. The units are not sorted single units (finding), with a median of 64 per mouse against the paper's 23. The 2 to 1 to 1 ratio of the statement holds in 25 of 31 sessions; H09 to H14 have no neutral CS.
deviations: The paper analyses sorted single units (Offline Sorter); the files' units are used as they are.

outcomes.notes: Needs the CRISPR and control groups and the tagged BLA-NAc and BLA-CeA neurons; every file gives the genotype as "Wild type" and none names the group or the Cav2-Cre injection site. The tagged neurons of fig4c-photoidentification are not known either (that claim is blocked, since the light blocks and the projections are not labelled).

No file gives the projection of each mouse, so the BLA-NAc and BLA-CeA counts cannot be split, but both are within 10% of 39 and 32 only if their total is within 63.9 to 78.1. With the Methods' rule and the fake-session test, block 1 taken as the fake session as the Methods order them, the total is 146 under reading (a) (all 5 and 10 ms pulses and the onsets of the 100 ms light events) and 133 under reading (b) (isolated 1 Hz pulses). With block 2 as the fake one it is 256 and 233; letting H31 to H42, where one block precedes the task, take either order gives at least 104 and 102; with a baseline rate of at least 0.3 Hz the lowest is 91. Every reading is above 78.1, so the counts cannot both match whatever the projections. But the fake-session test does not work as the Methods describe it. Without it, block 1 evokes a short-latency response in 1353 of 1902 units and block 2 in 1243 (reading a; 1474 and 1374 under reading b), and 88% of the units responsive to block 2 also respond to block 1. A session with the patch cord disconnected should evoke none, so either neither block is that fake session or the responses are light artefacts on units that are not sorted single units (finding). The 91 to 256 tagged units are then units that cross the threshold in one block and not the other, and their count does not test the claim. The files label neither the fake and real blocks nor the projection of each mouse, so the claim is blocked. Round 2 kept the outcome as not_reproduced and proposed blocked (metadata_insufficient); round 3 agreed.
deviations: Which light block is the fake session is not labelled. Block 1 is taken as the fake one (Methods, In vivo electrophysiology, "a phototagging session was conducted after a 'fake' phototagging session"); the reverse, and either order in H31 to H42, are run as readings and agree.
The files hold light events of 5, 10 and 100 ms and none of 1 s; the 100 ms events stand in for the long light in reading (a). Reading (b) does not use them and gives the same outcome.
The count is compared as a total, since the projection labels are missing.

outcomes.notes: Compares CRISPR and control; no file gives the group (see ed8d-reduced-basal-firing).

Run on the 1399 units of 24 mice with baseline of at least 0.3 Hz in sessions with all three CSs (163 units dropped for rate, 340 in the six sessions without neutral CSs, the whole of H17 for rate since its spikes stop at 249 s). With Ward linkage cut at 35% of the maximum distance, reading (a) gives 9, 12, 11, 12, 11, 10, 8 and 9 clusters for smoothing windows of 20 to 420 ms, and 6, 7, 6, 6 and 8 for 620 ms to 2 s; reading (b) gives 8 to 14 and never 7. Seven clusters come only under reading (a) with an 820 ms window. The paper's "smoothing factor of 0.85" is a MATLAB smoothdata setting whose window the paper does not give and that cannot be derived without MATLAB's heuristic, and the count moves with the window, so no reading has a defensible basis over another. The count also moves with the cut (14 at 25%, 13 at 30%, 10 at 35%, 7 at 40%, 5 at 50% for a 220 ms window). Without H22, H27, H34 and H39, whose CS alignment is not shown, seven clusters come under (a) at 420 ms and under (b) at 1020 ms and 2 s. Some clusters are single sessions (at 220 ms one cluster is 93% H27), so a count here would not show functional types. The question is for the paper's authors (finding). The units are not the paper's sorted single units, which alone could change the count.
deviations: The smoothing window is run from 20 ms to 2 s, as the paper gives only MATLAB's smoothing factor (Methods, Functional hierarchical clustering, "a Gaussian-weighted moving average with a smoothing factor of 0.85"); each CS trace is smoothed separately.

The six sessions without neutral CS trials (H09 to H14) are left out, since the clustered trace concatenates the three CSs (Methods, "Data from each experiment protocol (Sucrose CS, Neutral CS, Shock CS) were concatenated").

Compares CRISPR and control mice; no file gives the group. Its freezing part would also need the pose on the trial clock, which the files do not give; a fitted clock holds in 21 of 29 sessions (see fig5dh-behavior-clusters).

The pose has no timestamps, but a linear map of the trial clock onto the pose clock (offset and rate factor) fitted to the port entries holds in 21 of 29 sessions (best extra lag within 1 s in each third; 20 of the 21 factors between 0.9874 and 0.9885; median head-to-port distance at port entries 38 pixels against 105 over all frames). On the 1319 sucrose and 688 shock trials of those sessions (300 frames after each CS, 6264 tsfresh features, 5931 and 5927 kept), no reading gives both counts; each of the four meets one and not the other. With features z-scored and the installed scikit-learn defaults, the reading adopted, the kernel density has 7 peaks for sucrose and 3 for shock for all 5 seeds; with the 2020 defaults 7, 7, 8, 7, 8 and 4, 3, 4, 3, 3. With raw features it has 6 for sucrose and 5 for shock for all 5 seeds (installed defaults), and 7, 5, 7, 5, 6 and 5, 5, 5, 6, 7 (2020 defaults). So the sucrose count holds and the shock count does not under the z-scored features, and the reverse under the raw ones, and the outcome is partially_reproduced under every reading. The raw-feature counts are not stable. In the raw features the 3 largest features carry 95% (sucrose) and 98% (shock) of the variance and the 10 largest all of it; with the installed defaults an exact PCA in place of the randomized one gives 8 and 5, and multiplying each feature by 1 + 1e-9 noise gives 7 and 7. With z-scored features the same changes give 7 and 4, so the sucrose count stays at 7 and the shock count stays below 5. The run reviewed in round 2, with the same code on another runner, printed 7 and 5 (raw, installed defaults) and 9 and 4 (z-scored, installed defaults), which shows the same sensitivity. Without H08, H10 and H24, whose clock is checked least well (head-to-port distance under the map 29.0, 27.7 and 38.4 px against 35.1, 34.8 and 46.8 px over all frames), the adopted reading gives 5 and 4. The statement's "separate passive and active strategies" is not tested.
deviations: The pose is put on the trial clock by a linear map fitted to the port entries (nb.fit_pose_clock), since the files give only a start time and a nominal 15 frames per second; this is an assumption. H11, H14, H17, H23, H25, H29, H39 and H40, where the map does not hold, and H28 and H32, whose recorded session has no pose, are left out.
tsfresh 0.16.0 does not install with Python 3.13; tsfresh 0.21.2 with its comprehensive default feature set is used (6264 features per trial, the paper's "~6000").

Features that are not finite or are constant are dropped. Whether the features were scaled before PCA is not said (Methods, Unsupervised trial-based classification of behaviors); both are run and give the same outcome. z-scoring is the reading adopted for the measured counts, since on the raw features 10 features carry all the variance of the 30 PCs and the counts change with the PCA solver and with changes of 1e-9 in the features.

The criterion's "defaults of scikit-learn" are read as those of the installed release (1.9, PCA initialisation, automatic learning rate), as the criterion says; the defaults of the releases contemporary with tsfresh 0.16.0 (2020; random initialisation, learning rate 200) are run as a reading and give the same outcome. Under either set the tsfresh release is 0.21.2, not 0.16.0. The kernel density is seaborn's default (scipy gaussian_kde, Scott's bandwidth, a 200 by 200 grid reaching 3 bandwidths beyond the data); each local maximum is a watershed marker, so the count of maxima is the count of regions. Counting only maxima above 5% of the highest gives the same counts.

findings.statement: No file says which recorded mouse is in the CRISPR group and which in the control group, nor whether its Cav2-Cre was injected in the NAc or the CeA; every subject's genotype is "Wild type". The paper's electrophysiology findings compare the groups and the tagged projectors, so 13 of its claims cannot be tested, and the phototagging count cannot be split by projection. Neither the units table (spike times and a unit name), the electrodes table (location "unknown"), any other text field of the files, nor the archive's subject metadata (age, sex, species, genotype) holds such a label.

The units are not sorted single units, as the Methods describe (Offline Sorter). 21 of 31 sessions hold exactly 64 units on 32 channels, 1902 units in all against the paper's 685; in 1061 units more than 5% of inter-spike intervals are below 1 ms, and in each session 6 to 65% of spike samples recur in another unit. Both light blocks evoke a short-latency response in most of them (1353 and 1243 of 1902), so the light rule of the Methods with the fake-session test (91 to 256 tagged units, against 71 tagged neurons in the paper) cannot single out tagged neurons.
In H17 the spike times of all 64 units fall within the first 249 s of a 12118 s recording, while its trial events cover the whole session, so its spikes cannot be aligned with its trials.

The DeepLabCut pose has no timestamps, only a start time of 0 s and a nominal rate of 15 frames per second, and the mp4 videos give a constant 15 frames per second. Against the trial clock, port entries match the head's approach to the port at lags a median of 80 s and up to 192 s from zero that drift within 28 of 29 sessions. A linear map fitted to the port entries removes the drift in 21 sessions, with a rate factor of about 0.988 in 20 of them, as if the true frame rate were about 1.2% below 15; in 8 sessions no such map holds (lags of 2.8 to 19.2 s are left in some third). The videos of H07, H09 and H10 run 818 to 1528 s longer than their pose series, and that of H11 426 s longer; the others are within 10 s. Video timestamps, or the frame times of the original .asf files, would settle the alignment.

27 of the 31 ecephys files (all but H01, H02, H07 and H08) hold a stack of 8 to 42 confocal images (COFAImages) whose description names an Olympus FLUOVIEW file of the PVT. The images are named only by depth, with no channel, probe, stain or group label, so what they show cannot be read from the files.

Each session holds about 854 light events in two blocks of about 427, which fits the paper's "fake" phototagging session and the real one, but no label says which is which. In 12 sessions (H31 to H42) one block comes before the task, where the Methods put both after it. The two blocks evoke much the same short-latency responses (1353 and 1243 of 1902 units respond to the first and the second, and 88% of the units responsive to the second block also respond to the first), so neither behaves like a session with the patch cord disconnected. The files hold light events of 5, 10 and 100 ms and none of the 1 s light the Methods describe.
Six sessions (H09 to H14) hold 75 sucrose and 45 shock CSs and no neutral CS, while their session description says sucrose, shock and neutral CSs at 2 to 1 to 1.

The dandiset has recordings from 31 mice where the paper reports 30. For H28 and H32 the recorded session (Disc3, Disc5) is earlier than another discrimination day for which only pose is deposited (Disc4, Disc6), while the paper analyses only the last day.

The photometry files store one RoiResponseSeries at 60 Hz that interleaves the 415 nm frames, the 470 nm frames and a third, undescribed frame type; the channels can be told apart only from the LED event labels, and in one session (Mouse6, late sucrose) the labels move by one frame after a 2.3 ms frame interval while the data keep their order, so after it they mark the constant third frame type as 470 nm. In Mouse1's early airpuff session the last three cues come 4.7 and 7.4 s apart, one lasting 4.7 s. The cue events last 2 s where the Methods give a 4 s CS, and no event marks the US or says whether a cue was paired. In two airpuff sessions the lick label is on for most of the session.

Only the in vivo recordings of Figures 4 and 5 and the NT sensor photometry of Figure 3j-l are deposited. The behavior cohorts of Figures 1 and 2 and Extended Data Figure 10, the axon-terminal and somatic photometry with its head-fixed behavior (Figure 3b-f, Extended Data Figure 6), the anatomy and in situ data, the slice physiology and the sensor validation are not, so 19 of the paper's 39 findings in the claims file cannot be tested.

Question for the paper's authors. The functional clustering smooths each PSTH with MATLAB smoothdata and a smoothing factor of 0.85 (Methods, Functional hierarchical clustering). What window did that produce, and was the smoothing applied to each CS trace or to the concatenated trace? On the dandiset's units the number of clusters under the paper's cut-off ranges from 6 to 12 over windows of 20 ms to 2 s, not monotonically (9 at 20 ms, 12 at 60 ms, 6 at 620 ms, 8 at 2 s), with seven only at 820 ms.

Question for the paper's authors. The NT sensor residuals were "z-transformed using data a baseline window of -5 s to 0 s" (Methods, Fiber photometry, Data analysis). Was each trial z-scored against its own baseline, or against the session's baseline pooled over trials? The sucrose effect of Figure 3k reaches p = 0.0046 with each trial's baseline and all trials, and p >= 0.16 with the pooled baseline.

Question for the paper's authors. For the behavior clustering (Methods, Unsupervised trial-based classification of behaviors), were the tsfresh features scaled before PCA, and which scikit-learn release and t-SNE settings (perplexity, initialisation, learning rate) were used? On the dandiset's pose the sucrose and shock cluster counts range from 5 to 8 and 3 to 7 across these choices, the PCA solver and the seeds, and no reading gives 7 and 5 together. On unscaled features 10 features carry all the variance, and the counts change with the PCA solver and with changes of 1e-9 in the features, and between two runs of the same code on different runners.

disagreements.reason: Mice, 31, inside 30 +/- 3. Neurons, 1902 before the 0.3 Hz exclusion and 1739 after (cell 29), both far outside 685 +/- 68.5. Six sessions (H09 to H14) have no neutral CS, so the 2 to 1 to 1 ratio holds in only 25 of 31 sessions (cell 5).

verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The full executed notebook after the round-1 revision, with the conclusions and the summary, the helper module, the claims file and the attempt record, with the paper. Report in transcripts/000689/verifier-2-report.md.

disagreements.reason: Should be not_reproduced. The criterion says "Reproduced when the US comparison has p < 0.05 with late higher under every reading". It has one part, and only 2 of its 4 readings pass (cell 25). Those 2 are really one result, because AUC and mean give the same t and p. With the first 16 trials p = 0.093. The direction matches in all four readings, and the record can say so. The per-trial z-score is a reasonable assumption, but p = 0.0046 also depends on the trial-averaged regression, which has r = 0.25 to 0.75 in all four M-0 sessions and in M-1 late sucrose (cell 23); the pooled fit (r >= 0.94) gives p = 0.64 with all trials. The record reports this, but the conclusion depends on this one fit choice. The README sentence that the response rises after learning with p = 0.005 when all trials are used holds only under the per-trial z-score with the trial-averaged fit (session z-score p = 0.16, pooled fit p = 0.64). Cell 27, "partially reproduced, holds in 2 of its 4 readings", contradicts the criterion's "under every reading".

Block 1, taken as the fake session, gets a short-latency response from 1353 of 1902 units, and 88% of block-2 responders also respond to block 1 (cell 42). So it does not behave like a session with the patch cord disconnected, or the responses are light artefacts on unsorted channels. The 91 to 256 tagged units are then units that cross the threshold in one block but not the other, on units the record itself calls unsorted. Cell 43 says a count matching the paper was not expected. This does not test the claim, so it should be blocked (format_error, or the fake/real labels as metadata_insufficient). "Block 1 is the fake one" is an assumption not flagged assumed; all the orders were run, so this does not matter for the result.
